uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast prices are rising for UK households. The Bank of England targets it at 2%, so it steers interest rates, and benefit and pension increases are tied to it.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: Economists have warned of 5% UK inflation if a US diesel ban goes ahead, which turns attention to the fuel and energy lines of this release rather than the headline rate alone. The September figure reports prices as they stood while that ban was still a proposal, and it sets the baseline the warning is measured against.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight lending between US banks. Its decisions pass through to mortgages, corporate borrowing and the dollar worldwide.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee meets with its two mandates pulling apart: the Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected, days after traders had priced in a run of rate hikes. It also decides under open pressure — Trump demanded Powell resign even after a watchdog cleared him over the Fed's building renovations.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets roughly every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its decisions reach borrowing costs across the bloc, and the euro moves with them.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, the highest level in three years, and Lagarde has painted a darkening picture of inflation in Europe. The European Central Bank now decides whether that jump calls for a rate hike, and this meeting settles how it answers the pressure.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the cost of servicing one of the world's largest government debts.
boj-2026-10.recent: Japanese yields jumped on 1 October and deepened a global bond sell-off, which puts Japan's own debt market at the centre of the move rather than at its edge. The board meets with that selloff still running, and its decision settles how much of the rise in Japanese yields it is prepared to leave standing.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. That rate feeds through to British mortgages, savings and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee decides whether to hold, raise or cut the rate that prices mortgages and business loans. It does so as the question among central banks has turned to hikes: inflation is reported as stubborn from Europe to Australia, and government bond yields are at their highest since 2007.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate that US banks charge each other overnight. Its decisions feed into borrowing costs worldwide, and the dollar moves with them.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Hiring has stalled: the Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected, days after traders had priced in a run of Fed rate hikes. The committee decides with that gap unresolved, and with Trump demanding Powell resign even though a watchdog cleared him over the building renovations.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The yearly meeting of leaders from 19 major economies plus the European Union and African Union, hosted by a rotating presidency that sets the agenda. Its members produce about 85% of world output, and it decides by consensus.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Rubio has invited Putin, who is wanted by the ICC, to Miami, and the Kremlin is weighing the invitation. Its answer sets what the summit is about before any agenda item: whether the other leaders sit at a table with him, and whether a host's invitation counts for more than the court's.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets roughly every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its decisions reach mortgages, business loans and government borrowing across the bloc.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, the highest level in three years, and Lagarde has painted a darkening picture of prices in Europe. That keeps a rate hike on the table, and this meeting settles whether borrowing costs across the bloc rise to meet it.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its vote feeds through to UK mortgage and savings rates, the cost of government borrowing, and the pound.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee decides after a global bond sell-off took average government yields to their highest since 2007, with central banks from the Fed to the RBI pressed on inflation. The vote settles whether the rate it controls moves with that market or holds against it.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, Japanese government bond yields and the vast sums Japanese investors hold abroad.
boj-2026-12.recent: Japanese government bond yields jumped as a global sell-off deepened, so the Bank of Japan meets with its own debt market already repricing ahead of it. The decision settles whether the policy rate follows what bondholders have demanded, in a country whose government carries the heaviest debt load in the rich world.

fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.standing: The monthly consumer price index from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the main gauge of US inflation. It tracks what households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, and it feeds interest-rate policy, bond yields and Social Security adjustments.
fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.recent: This release lands between two readings that pull in opposite directions. The Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs in September against 90,000 expected, while an energy shock lifted euro zone inflation to 3.8% from 3.2% in the same month. The report shows whether US prices followed Europe's up while hiring stalled.

fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.standing: The Producer Price Index, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, measures what US producers receive for goods and services. It shows cost pressure before it reaches shop prices, and bond yields and the dollar move with it.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of what American shops, restaurants and online sellers took in. Consumer spending is about two-thirds of the US economy, so the figure moves growth forecasts, Treasury yields and the dollar.
